pages.x: After the Seven Years' War, Britain taxed its American colonies to help pay its debts. The colonists, who had no members in Parliament, protested. In 1773 men dressed as Mohawks threw 342 chests of tea into Boston harbour. Britain closed the port and sent troops.

On 19 April 1775 British soldiers marched out of Boston to seize the colonists' weapons at Concord. Militiamen, warned in the night by riders such as Paul Revere, met them at Lexington. Shots were fired, and the war had begun.

On 4 July 1776 the Continental Congress in Philadelphia adopted a Declaration of Independence, written mostly by Thomas Jefferson. It said that all men are created equal, with rights to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness, though Jefferson, like many who signed it, owned slaves.

General George Washington lost New York and retreated across New Jersey. On Christmas night 1776 he led his freezing army across the icy Delaware River and surprised the Hessian soldiers at Trenton. It kept the revolution alive.

In 1777 a British army marching south from Canada was surrounded and forced to surrender at Saratoga. The victory persuaded France to join the war on the American side in 1778, and Spain and the Dutch followed.

Washington's army spent the winter of 1777 at Valley Forge, short of food, clothes and shoes, and some 2,000 men died of disease. A Prussian officer, Baron von Steuben, drilled the survivors into a real army.

In 1781 the British general Cornwallis dug in at Yorktown, in Virginia, waiting for the navy. A French fleet blocked the bay, and the American and French armies trapped him. On 19 October he surrendered about 8,000 men. The story goes that his band played The World Turned Upside Down.
In the Treaty of Paris of 1783 Britain recognised the United States, with land as far west as the Mississippi. In 1789 Washington became the first president under a new Constitution.

The revolution made the first large modern republic and spread the ideas that government rests on the consent of the governed and that people have rights no ruler can take away. Those ideas fed the French Revolution, and in time the struggles against slavery and for equal rights in America itself.
